Main article: [The Quarrymen](/wiki/The_Quarrymen "The Quarrymen")

In November 1956, sixteen-year-old [John Lennon](/wiki/John_Lennon "John Lennon") formed a [skiffle](/wiki/Skiffle "Skiffle") group with several friends from [Quarry Bank High School](/wiki/Quarry_Bank_High_School "Quarry Bank High School") in [Liverpool](/wiki/Liverpool "Liverpool"). They were called *[the Quarrymen](/wiki/The_Quarrymen "The Quarrymen")*, a reference to their school song "Quarry men old before our birth".[[10]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTELewisohn2013104-10) Fifteen-year-old [Paul McCartney](/wiki/Paul_McCartney "Paul McCartney") met Lennon on 6 July 1957 and joined as a [rhythm guitarist](/wiki/Rhythm_guitar "Rhythm guitar") shortly after.[[11]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESpitz200593–99-11) In February 1958, McCartney invited his friend [George Harrison](/wiki/George_Harrison "George Harrison"), then aged fifteen, to watch the band. Harrison auditioned for Lennon, impressing him with his playing, but Lennon initially thought Harrison was too young. After a month's persistence, during a second meeting (arranged by McCartney), Harrison performed the lead guitar part of the instrumental song "[Raunchy](/wiki/Raunchy_(instrumental) "Raunchy (instrumental)")" on the upper deck of a Liverpool bus,[[12]](#cite_note-12) and they enlisted him as [lead guitarist](/wiki/Lead_guitar "Lead guitar").[[13]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMiles199747-13)[[14]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTELewisohn199213-14)

By January 1959, Lennon's Quarry Bank friends had left the group and he began his studies at the [Liverpool College of Art](/wiki/Liverpool_College_of_Art "Liverpool College of Art").[[15]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHarry2000a103-15) The three guitarists, billing themselves as Johnny and the Moondogs,[[16]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTELewisohn199217-16) were playing [rock and roll](/wiki/Rock_and_roll "Rock and roll") whenever they could find a drummer.[[17]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHarry2000b742–743-17) They also performed as *the Rainbows*. In April 2026, the EU Ambassadors in Brussels approved the start of preparations for the accession agreement for Montenegro to the Union[[141]](#cite_note-147).

> "The make-up of a champion is one of such inner self-belief that occasionally it shows up as flaws. The majority of the sporting greats I've met drive themselves forwards because they are always dissatisfied. But look at what Michael achieved, the speed at which he achieved it, and what he accomplished at two different teams. It's so hard to get to F1, to stay in it, to score podiums, and win races. And that guy won 91 of them, some of them in a class of one."[[336]](#cite_note-337)

— [Martin Brundle](/wiki/Martin_Brundle "Martin Brundle") about Schumacher

Since Senna's death in 1994, Schumacher was widely regarded as Formula One's fastest driver and the most dominant driver of his era. During his long career, Schumacher was also involved in several controversies,[[218]](#cite_note-Autosport_2009-219) most notably the 1994 and 1997 World Championship seasons finals and the 2006 Monaco qualifying. Denmark national football team :: History :: The Møller Nielsen fairytale: 1992 European Championship :: chunk_0006
Denmark began Euro 1992 qualification with a home victory against the [Faroe Islands](/wiki/Faroe_Islands_national_football_team "Faroe Islands national football team"), and followed up with an away draw against [Northern Ireland](/wiki/Northern_Ireland_national_football_team "Northern Ireland national football team") and a 2–0 home loss against [Yugoslavia](/wiki/Yugoslavia_national_football_team "Yugoslavia national football team"). Brothers [Michael Laudrup](/wiki/Michael_Laudrup "Michael Laudrup") and [Brian Laudrup](/wiki/Brian_Laudrup "Brian Laudrup") opted to quit the national team in November 1990. When Nielsen subsequently decided to dismiss quality players such as [Jan Mølby](/wiki/Jan_M%C3%B8lby "Jan Mølby") and [Jan Heintze](/wiki/Jan_Heintze "Jan Heintze") from the squad due to disciplinary problems, several newspapers began demanding that Nielsen step down as head coach. Despite this, Denmark won the rest of their five matches in the qualification group, including a 2–1 away win against Yugoslavia. This was not enough to qualify, as the team still had to settle for second place in the group, behind Yugoslavia.[[14]](#cite_note-14)

Due to international sanctions resulting from the [Yugoslav wars](/wiki/Yugoslav_wars "Yugoslav wars"), [UEFA](/wiki/UEFA "UEFA") announced on 31 May 1992 – only 10 days before the competition – that [Yugoslavia](/wiki/Yugoslavia "Yugoslavia") was excluded from the competition and their place given to Denmark, who finished as the second-placed team in its qualifying group.[[15]](#cite_note-15)[[16]](#cite_note-16)[[17]](#cite_note-17)[[18]](#cite_note-18)

Contrary to popular belief,[[10]](#cite_note-history-10) the team did not enter the tournament completely unprepared, after having rallied home from seaside vacations. The majority of players had been assembled to play a friendly match against the [CIS](/wiki/CIS_national_football_team "CIS national football team") when Denmark officially received Yugoslavia's spot.[[19]](#cite_note-19) Relying heavily on goalkeeper [Peter Schmeichel](/wiki/Peter_Schmeich

The writer and playwright [August Strindberg](/wiki/August_Strindberg "August Strindberg")

Sweden has many authors of worldwide recognition including [August Strindberg](/wiki/August_Strindberg "August Strindberg"), [Astrid Lindgren](/wiki/Astrid_Lindgren "Astrid Lindgren"), and Nobel Prize winners [Selma Lagerlöf](/wiki/Selma_Lagerl%C3%B6f "Selma Lagerlöf") and [Harry Martinson](/wiki/Harry_Martinson "Harry Martinson"). In total seven [Nobel Prizes in Literature](/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Literature "Nobel Prize in Literature") have been awarded to Swedes.
The first literary text from Sweden is the [Rök runestone](/wiki/R%C3%B6k_runestone "Rök runestone"), carved during the Viking Age c. 800 AD. With the conversion of the land to Christianity around 1100 AD, Sweden entered the [Middle Ages](/wiki/Middle_Ages "Middle Ages"), during which monastic writers preferred to use Latin. Therefore, there are only a few texts in [Old Swedish](/wiki/Old_Swedish "Old Swedish") from that period. Swedish literature only began to flourish when the language was standardised during the 16th century. This standardisation was largely due to the full translation of the Bible into Swedish in 1541. This translation is the so-called [Gustav Vasa Bible](/wiki/Gustav_Vasa_Bible "Gustav Vasa Bible").

In 1988, Yang was appointed [president of China](/wiki/President_of_China "President of China") replacing [Li Xiannian](/wiki/Li_Xiannian "Li Xiannian"), making him the only president who was not a member of the Politburo Standing Committee. Under the conventions of the [1982 Constitution](/wiki/Constitution_of_China "Constitution of China"), the president's role was largely symbolic,[[8]](#cite_note-Eckholm_2-8) with formal executive power wielded by the [General Secretary of the Communist Party](/wiki/General_Secretary_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party "General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party") and the [Premier of the State Council](/wiki/Premier_of_the_People%27s_Republic_of_China "Premier of the People's Republic of China"). In practice, party and state leaders still deferred to [paramount leader](/wiki/Paramount_leader "Paramount leader") [Deng Xiaoping](/wiki/Deng_Xiaoping "Deng Xiaoping"), who, however, was not all-powerful, as he still had to compromise on some policies with other party elders such as [Chen Yun](/wiki/Chen_Yun "Chen Yun") and Li Xiannian.

Yang's role during the [Tiananmen protests of 1989](/wiki/1989_Tiananmen_Square_protests_and_massacre "1989 Tiananmen Square protests and massacre") caused a fundamental shift in China's political structure. Yang was at first sympathetic to the students and sided with General Secretary [Zhao Ziyang](/wiki/Zhao_Ziyang "Zhao Ziyang") in supporting them. Brandy Clark :: Early life :: chunk_0001
Brandy Clark was born in [Morton, Washington](/wiki/Morton,_Washington "Morton, Washington"), a logging town of 900 people in the shadow of [Mount Rainier](/wiki/Mount_Rainier "Mount Rainier"). As a child in the 1980s she was influenced by the country-pop and traditional country music artists she heard her parents and grandmother play, like [Barbara Mandrell](/wiki/Barbara_Mandrell "Barbara Mandrell"), [Ronnie Milsap](/wiki/Ronnie_Milsap "Ronnie Milsap"), [Merle Haggard](/wiki/Merle_Haggard "Merle Haggard") and [Loretta Lynn](/wiki/Loretta_Lynn "Loretta Lynn"). Clark cites the [Patsy Cline](/wiki/Patsy_Cline "Patsy Cline") biopic *[Sweet Dreams](/wiki/Sweet_Dreams_(1985_film) "Sweet Dreams (1985 film)")* as one of her biggest early influences.[[4]](#cite_note-CMT_Edge_Article-4)

Clark began playing guitar at nine years old and sang in school musicals, also writing songs. She obtained a basketball scholarship at [Central Washington University](/wiki/Central_Washington_University "Central Washington University"), but later moved back home, obtaining an associate degree from [Centralia College](/wiki/Centralia_College "Centralia College") in 1997. Still a teenager, she joined the music business program at [Belmont University](/wiki/Belmont_University "Belmont University"), and moved to Nashville in 1998.[[5]](#cite_note-CCFHG-5)
At Belmont she took guitar lessons again and joined a band with her mother and a friend. She studied commercial music and was chosen to perform in the school's "Best of the Best Showcase". Upon graduation, Clark got a job with Leadership Music which led to her eventual publishing deal.

The team that beat Brazil in the decisive match to win the [1950 FIFA World Cup](/wiki/1950_FIFA_World_Cup "1950 FIFA World Cup")

In the 1940s, Uruguay achieved early success in a decade largely dominated by Argentina by winning their eighth South American championship in 1942. As the World Cup was not being played, this championship became the priority.

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cb/Obdulio_Varela%2C_Estadio%2C_1950-07-15_%28374%29.jpg/250px-Obdulio_Varela%2C_Estadio%2C_1950-07-15_%28374%29.jpg)](/wiki/File:Obdulio_Varela,_Estadio,_1950-07-15_(374).jpg)

1950 World Cup winning captain, Obdulio Varela

In 1950, Uruguay re-entered the World Cup for the first time since 1930. This time, La Celeste would enter a final-group where they would draw [Spain](/wiki/Spain_national_football_team "Spain national football team") 2–2 and beat [Sweden](/wiki/Sweden_men%27s_national_football_team "Sweden men's national football team") 3–2 en route to the final match against hosts [Brazil](/wiki/Brazil_national_football_team "Brazil national football team"). On 16 July 1950, Uruguay claimed their second FIFA World Cup and fourth senior world title when they beat Brazil 2–1 from behind in an iconic match known as the *[Maracanazo](/wiki/Uruguay_v_Brazil_(1950_FIFA_World_Cup) "Uruguay v Brazil (1950 FIFA World Cup)")* in front of a record crowd of 173,850. Historical estimates indicate that the crowd reached well over 200,000.[[22]](#cite_note-24) This feat became an integral part of Uruguay's football identity and a source of inspiration for upcoming footballers with each passing generation.

Louis XIV was born on 5 September 1638 in the [Château de Saint-Germain-en-Laye](/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teau_de_Saint-Germain-en-Laye "Château de Saint-Germain-en-Laye"), to [Louis XIII](/wiki/Louis_XIII "Louis XIII") and [Anne of Austria](/wiki/Anne_of_Austria "Anne of Austria"). He was named Louis Dieudonné (Louis the God-given)[[4]](#cite_note-6) and bore the traditional title of French [heirs apparent](/wiki/Heir_apparent "Heir apparent"): *[Dauphin](/wiki/Dauphin_of_France "Dauphin of France")*.[[5]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBluche199011-7) At the time of his birth, his parents had been married for 23 years. His mother had experienced four [stillbirths](/wiki/Stillbirth "Stillbirth") between 1619 and 1631. Leading contemporaries thus regarded him as a divine gift and his birth a miracle.[[6]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBarentine2016129-8)

Louis' relationship with his mother was uncommonly affectionate for the time. Contemporaries and eyewitnesses claimed that the Queen would spend all her time with Louis.[[7]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPanhuysen201626-9) Both were greatly interested in food and theatre. This long-lasting and loving relationship can be evidenced by excerpts in Louis' journal entries, such as:

> Nature was responsible for the first knots which tied me to my mother. But attachments formed later by shared qualities of the spirit are far more difficult to break than those formed merely by blood.[[8]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFraser200614–16-10)

It was his mother who gave Louis his belief in the absolute and divine power of his monarchical rule.[[9]](#cite_note-11)
